rules.statement: Persistence write operations that a handler composes with other writes must stage their changes on the caller-supplied store manager / unit of work rather than opening and saving their own, so the calling handler controls the transaction boundary.
rules.why: A seam that owns its own unit of work cannot be composed atomically with related writes (e.g. creating related rows or audit/ownership records) in a single transaction.
rules.check: Look for store or service write methods that create their own store manager/DbContext and call SaveChanges internally when they are invoked from a handler that performs other related writes; they should accept the caller's unit of work and only stage changes.

rules.statement: When creating an entity that requires companion rows (e.g. a local account with its principal and self-issued identity), stage all of them together in one unit of work instead of creating the companions lazily on a later read path.
rules.why: Lazy creation leaves a window where the entity exists without its required companions, forcing special cases and scattering provisioning across read-ish paths.
rules.check: Look for create paths that write only the primary row and rely on get-or-create logic in later read/login/metadata paths to materialize required related rows.

rules.statement: A password reset or credential change must rehash the credential and rotate the account's security stamp so outstanding sessions and tokens are invalidated.
rules.why: Without rotating the security stamp, sessions and tokens issued under the old credential remain valid after a reset.
rules.check: Look for password reset/change code paths that update the password hash without also rotating the security stamp.

rules.statement: Keep credential hashing, security-stamp rotation and account id generation behind the account store/seam abstraction rather than calling password hashers or mutating credential fields directly from management handlers.
rules.why: Leaking hashing and stamping logic into the management layer prevents an alternative account backend (e.g. one over ASP.NET Core Identity) from owning them.
rules.check: Look for management/API handlers that call IPasswordHasher or set security stamps or password hashes on account entities directly.

rules.statement: Server/system-only subject metadata must only be writable through administrator-gated endpoints, never through end-user-accessible paths.
rules.why: SystemMetadata is a server/admin trust boundary; end-user writes would let subjects tamper with server-asserted data.
rules.check: Look for new endpoints or code paths that write system metadata and are reachable by end users or lack administrator authorization.

rules.statement: Management endpoints whose backing service comes from an optional, opt-in package must respond 501 Not Implemented when that service is not registered, rather than throwing or returning 500.
rules.why: The feature is opt-in; a missing registration is an unsupported capability, not a server fault.
rules.check: Look for endpoints that resolve an optional service and throw or return 500/404 when it is not registered instead of 501.
